conclusion: The tiny-body steady purchase workload is dominated by shared driver bookkeeping across publication/command application, planning, and admission/reservation work. Publication is the largest robust eight-worker exclusive bucket (~29%), not a single planner hotspot. More workers increase total cycles/request while throughput flattens after four workers.
scope: Current uncommitted source, warmed fixed-world independent purchases, 1000 slots, work=0, dispatch width16. Direct .system(sync_fn) API fix preserved. No optimization or commit performed.

provenance.actual_attribution_build_command: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/profiling-fp RUSTFLAGS='-C force-frame-pointers=yes' cargo build --workspace --examples --profile bench -j20 --message-format=json
provenance.runner_static_build_command_caveat: profile-engine historical build_command field is not the actual FP command; use attribution manifest.

mechanism_priority: Map-key hashing (Invocation,TypeId,Entity,SystemId) is substantial and distributed across phases; component-payload hashing is a much smaller separately identified category. Generic untyped hashing remains unresolved.

Publication freshness checking, derived ownership bookkeeping, command application, write reconciliation and COW cloning are all material subcosts; do not treat total publication as pure revision lookup.
Planning combines row/join enumeration, dependency/key/access collection and memo checks; a substantial inlined planner remainder prevents a single exact leaf diagnosis.

Admission/reservation bookkeeping and execution/completion contexts also consume material CPU; eight-worker driver fraction ~77-79% supports a shared serial-work explanation for poor tiny-body scaling, not a universal planner bottleneck.
limits: Throughput and hardware counters use ordinary optimized binary; attribution uses same optimized feature/source graph with force-frame-pointers=yes, which may perturb layout/timing. FP timings are not replacement throughput numbers.

Two independent100-round recordings per async/sync and one/eight-worker configuration; not a confidence interval. All percentages are sampled user CPU cycles across driver and workers, not wall-time fractions.
Each sample belongs to one nearest recognized actual outer-function stage; nested generic type names ignored. Residual other/unknown remains explicit.
Admission category includes reservation insertion/conflict checks AND release after publication.

Worker row execution and completion/dispatch boundaries depend on compiler inlining. Combine them with resolved kernel-body frames for a safer execution-path total; resolved kernel bodies below0.3% do not prove all business logic below0.3%.

Mechanism categories are a separate dimension overlapping the stage table; do not add mechanism percentages to stage percentages. Generic Hasher::write samples without typed caller remain unknown key/payload.
revision_for_entity symbols may be identical-code-folded to a Stamp specialization; this does not establish active Stamp workload or that exact component type dominates.
Publication includes command application from all measured phases including base input application; subcosts with ambiguous inlining remain other within stage.
Production admission/publication diagnostic timers are elapsed instrumented regions, not mutually exclusive CPU ownership; do not add them to sampled percentages or infer wall-time shares.
